sections.h2: Jefferson County and why its bills run high
sections.html:
Charles Town is the seat of Jefferson County, a 212-square-mile county in the Eastern Panhandle that borders Maryland to the north and Virginia to the east and southwest. Charles Town and Ranson are the cities, and Bolivar, Harpers Ferry and Shepherdstown are the towns. Growth comes mainly from people who commute to the Washington area, which is why values here, and the bills that follow from them, look different from the rest of the state.

The county has five magisterial districts: Charles Town, Harpers Ferry, Kabletown, Middleway and Shepherdstown. Rural parcels outside the cities and towns are Class III or Class II depending on use, and parcels inside a municipality that are not owner-occupied are Class IV. Check where your parcel sits before you compare a bill with a neighbor's.

Many residents live in Jefferson County and work in Washington or Northern Virginia, so demand follows the commute. The MARC Brunswick Line runs from Martinsburg into Washington, with West Virginia stops at Harpers Ferry (120 Potomac Street) and Duffields (5057 Flowing Springs Road). West Virginia riders pay a surcharge on top of the base fare.

Older properties in Harpers Ferry, Shepherdstown and Charles Town can come with preservation questions, aging systems and unusual lot lines. Sellers with a house like that often prefer a buyer who accepts it in present condition.

The Sheriff's Tax Office at 110 N. George Street in Charles Town collects the tax but does not set the rate or value property. More than 46,000 bills are processed each year. Mail goes to P.O. Box 9, Charles Town, WV 25414, and the phone is 304-728-3220.

  • The office does not accept credit cards, and checks should show the tax ticket number.
  • An online tax search and payment system is available, along with a payment portal run by Point and Pay.
  • Tax bills are mailed around mid-year.

Real property gets a fresh appraisal at least every third year, and the County Commission, not the sheriff, determines the rate.

Each year's real estate bill is split into two payments. Paying one on or before its date keeps the 2.5 percent discount.

DateWhat it means
September 1First half due for the 2.5 percent discount
October 1First half becomes delinquent and 9 percent annual interest begins
March 1Second half due for the 2.5 percent discount
April 1Second half becomes delinquent
May and SeptemberDelinquent lists published in the Spirit of Jefferson

The county purposes levy for the 2025 tax year is $20,020,050, and none of it comes from excess levies. Excess levies are voter-approved additions on top of regular rates, and Jefferson County has none on the county side.

That does not mean a bill here is low. Voters can still approve school board excess levies, and higher home values mean a larger bill at the same rate. West Virginia's regular ceilings for Class II property inside a municipality add up to $1.00 per $100 of assessed value. Confirm the actual levy for your district with the sheriff, and ask whether a school board excess levy is on the ticket for the year you plan to sell.

For sellers, the higher the value, the more a late payment costs in interest at 9 percent a year, and the more a missed homestead filing matters. Owners 65 or older may exclude the first $20,000 of assessed value if they filed.

Start with a call to the assessor's office, and if the value still looks wrong, bring evidence such as recent sales of similar homes or repair estimates for a damaged structure. Formal challenges are heard by the County Commission in its Board of Equalization and Review role. It opens February 1 and wraps up before March. To contest the board's ruling, petition the Office of Tax Appeals by March 31. Call the assessor's office to confirm hearing arrangements for the year. The buyer gets reassessed on the next cycle regardless, so if you are about to sell, appeal only when the number is plainly off.

sections.h2: Delinquent property and a cash sale
sections.html:
A law passed in 2022 placed the sale of delinquent properties with the West Virginia State Auditor. A seller with unpaid tax should ask the Sheriff's Tax Office where the parcel stands before the lists are published in May and September.

One way around all that is a cash sale, where the title company pays the tax at the closing table. We buy houses as-is across Jefferson County, from Charles Town and Ranson to Shepherdstown, and you can reach us at (424) 435-2326. Nothing needs repairing, clearing out or staging beforehand, and the written offer comes with a plain explanation.

sections.h2: What to do before you list
sections.html:
Your first call goes to the Sheriff's Tax Office, 304-728-3220, to learn what is paid and what is open for the year. Check whether the last bill went to the right address, since bills are mailed around mid-year and a ticket that never reached a vacant or inherited house is still owed, and interest keeps running on it. Then look up the current assessment, because the county revisits real property at least every three years and your value may have moved since you bought.

If you hold the homestead exemption, let the title agent know. Owners 65 or older who filed may exclude $20,000 of assessed value, and a buyer will ask how the bill changes after the sale.

Last, have the title company request a payoff on anything still open. With no cards taken at the counter, you can pay by check with the ticket number written on it, or leave the balance for the title company to settle from your proceeds.

Real estate is only part of the Sheriff's job. Personal property tax on vehicles, boats, livestock, farm equipment and machinery is due September 1 and March 1, and paying it is a condition of renewing a vehicle registration with the state. If you are leaving the county, clear those bills so a registration is not held up later.

  • Delinquent personal property accrues penalties, and its delinquent list runs in May.
  • Real estate tax runs separately, and any balance comes out of proceeds at closing.
  • Recording a deed draws a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 of value.
  • A transfer worth $1,000 or less is not a taxable document.

Because the real property assessment is revisited at least every three years, a house you bought some time ago may carry a value that has moved. Look up the current assessment before listing. A cash buyer takes the property as it stands and walks through the paperwork with you.

faqs.q: When are Jefferson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due September 1 and March 1, each carrying a 2.5 percent discount when made by its date. Unpaid tax gains 9 percent annual interest, and the first half is delinquent as of October 1.

faqs.q: Does the Jefferson County Sheriff take credit cards?
faqs.a: No, the Sheriff's Tax Office takes no credit cards. You can pay in person or by mail, and an online payment portal exists as well.

faqs.q: How often does Jefferson County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Real property is reviewed at least once every three years under the state's reassessment rule, and some properties more often.

faqs.q: Who sells delinquent tax properties in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: A 2022 law moved sales of delinquent properties to the West Virginia State Auditor.

faqs.q: What is the Jefferson County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Resident owners aged 65 or older can exclude the first $20,000 of assessed value. Owners certified permanently and totally disabled are covered too.
